Every agent failure-attribution benchmark scores a diagnosis by how well it agrees with a human label for "which step went wrong". **ReplayRCA** replaces the label with an outcome: restore the environment to the state before the suspected step, swap in the proposed action, let the *same* agent continue, and see whether the run now succeeds. The diagnosis is right exactly when the correction flips the result.

That single change makes the metric harder to game, because a plausible-sounding explanation no longer earns credit. It also forces a control that rerun-based evaluation usually omits: a **paired placebo** that replays the agent's own original action through the same restoration mechanism. Without it, an agent that simply retries well gets credited to the diagnoser. The resulting score — *causal repair* — is the continuation success rate minus the placebo's.

## The Result That Matters

The benchmark runs on **OpsWorld**, a deterministic procedurally generated back-office environment with 15 tools, three task families, six difficulty levels, and a multimodal top level involving QR codes and handwriting. On **62 calibrated systematic failures**, the best of 13 frontier models (Grok 4.7) reaches a causal repair of **+51.3 points**.

The interesting part is what happens below the leader. The top eight models are **statistically indistinguishable**, the flagship models of the two largest vendors rank **8th and 12th**, and **5 items are repaired by no model at all**. Forcing a strong model to intervene at the last step — the shortcut that annotation-based attribution benchmarks reward — costs it **17.1 points**.

## Autopsy Is Not Oversight

On **87 live runs**, the two best supervisors are tied, and one of them is a small open-weight model (DeepSeek V4.1 Flash). The model that ranks among the best post-hoc diagnosers (**GPT-6.1 Sol**) is the **weakest** live one, at **-14.5 points on the same runs (p = 0.002)**.

The lesson is uncomfortable for anyone staffing an agent oversight pipeline with the same model used for post-hoc debugging: explaining a failure after the fact is not the same capability as preventing it mid-run. In the live track, the supervisor never learns whether the run will fail, and successful runs are mixed in so false alarms are measured too — conditions no retrospective trace provides.

Environment and evaluation code are released. The caveat is that OpsWorld's released instances and generator structure remain learnable, so the numbers will need reproducing on environments agents have not seen.

Paper: [arXiv:2610.41025](https://arxiv.org/abs/2610.41025)
